title: C++ Fundamental Data Types
learningObjectives: Explain the key idea in c++ fundamental data types.
Identify suitable syntax and type/value rules.
Trace each example and predict the result.
Use the concept in a small practical program.
Avoid a common mistake related to initialization, constness or type choice.

understand.concept: Data types define the kinds of values an object can store and the operations available for those values. Fundamental types include integers, floating-point numbers, characters, booleans and void. Choose types according to the meaning and range of data, and avoid assuming every type has identical size on every platform.
understand.whyItMatters: These fundamentals appear in nearly every C++ program and help make code predictable, readable and correct.
understand.analogy: Think of a labeled container: its label identifies what it is meant to hold, and its rules determine what can be put inside or changed.
understand.analogyLimit: Real C++ types have language-defined rules, conversions, representation and lifetime that a physical container analogy cannot capture.
understand.explain:
## Common types
`int` represents integer values; `double` represents floating-point values; `char` represents character-sized data; and `bool` represents true or false. Use `std::string` for text strings in typical C++ programs.

## Type and range
Types have defined properties but sizes and ranges can vary across implementations. Use fixed-width integer types from `<cstdint>` when a specific width is needed and supported.

## Type choice
Choose a type that matches the data's meaning. Avoid using floating-point for exact decimal currency arithmetic without an appropriate representation strategy. Do not mix types casually; conversions can change values.

examples.title: Integer count
examples.explanation: An integer stores a whole-number value.

examples.title: Floating-point measurement
examples.explanation: double can represent fractional values, with binary floating-point precision limits.

examples.title: Character and boolean
examples.code: #include <iostream>\nint main(){ char grade{'A'}; bool passed{true}; std::cout << grade << ' ' << passed; }
examples.explanation: A character stores a character value and bool stores true/false; default stream formatting prints true as 1.

examples.title: Text with string
examples.explanation: std::string is a standard-library type used for text.

examples.title: Type size check
examples.explanation: sizeof reports size in bytes; do not assume int has the same size on every target.

practise.guidedTask: Review the first example. Predict the value/output, then modify the code and explain the change. Compile and run it if a C++ compiler is available.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program that stores several values relevant to a simple real-world task, uses appropriate types and produces a readable result. Include two tests and explain your type choices.
hints: Use names that explain the value.
Use const when a value should not be reassigned.
Choose types based on meaning and range.
Do not assume type sizes are identical across platforms.

questions.prompt: Why initialize a variable when declaring it?
options: To give it a known starting value
To make the variable name longer
questions.answer: To give it a known starting value
questions.explanation: Initialization establishes the initial value and prevents use of an indeterminate local value.

options: The object cannot be modified through that name after initialization
The value is always stored as text
questions.answer: The object cannot be modified through that name after initialization
questions.explanation: const prevents modification through that name.

questions.prompt: Which type is commonly used for true/false values?
Which type is commonly used for fractional measurements?
What is a good type-selection practice?
options: Choose a type based on value meaning and range
Assume all types have identical size
questions.answer: Choose a type based on value meaning and range
questions.explanation: Types differ in representation, range and operations.
